metadata.chapter_title: Chapter XXVI: Rama's Mission Fulfilled

text: Suddenly Rama darted forward. He drew his bow and shot a swift arrow, which smote off one of Ravana's ten heads, but immediately another appeared in its place.[346] Then the hero seized the flaming weapon which Brahma had created for the protection of the gods; with unerring aim he discharged it in flaming splendour; it struck the demon; it cleft in twain his heart of iron. Roaring in his fierce agony Ravana fell ponderously upon the plain and immediately expired. So was the enemy of gods and men put to death by peerless Rama.
chapter_title: Chapter XXVI: Rama's Mission Fulfilled
source_reference: Indian Myth and Legend (Mackenzie 1913), Ch 27, Para 68

metadata.chapter_title: Chapter XXVI: Rama's Mission Fulfilled

text: Celestial music was heard in heaven and flowers fell upon the plain of victory: a voice came down the wind, saying: “_O victor of truth and righteousness, thy task is now ended._”
chapter_title: Chapter XXVI: Rama's Mission Fulfilled
source_reference: Indian Myth and Legend (Mackenzie 1913), Ch 27, Para 69

metadata.chapter_title: Chapter XXVI: Rama's Mission Fulfilled

text: The Rakshasa hosts broke in flight when Ravana fell, and Rama entered the city in triumph. Bibhishana burned the body of his fallen brother, and performed the funeral rites. Thereafter he was proclaimed King of Lanka.
chapter_title: Chapter XXVI: Rama's Mission Fulfilled
source_reference: Indian Myth and Legend (Mackenzie 1913), Ch 27, Para 70

metadata.chapter_title: Chapter XXVI: Rama's Mission Fulfilled

text: When peace was restored, Rama commanded that Sita should be brought forth. She was carried towards the plain concealed in a litter, and all the Apes gathered round to behold her, whereat Rama requested her to alight and walk towards him, and she did so. With folded hands she approached her husband and knelt at his feet, weeping tears of joy.
chapter_title: Chapter XXVI: Rama's Mission Fulfilled
source_reference: Indian Myth and Legend (Mackenzie 1913), Ch 27, Para 71

metadata.chapter_title: Chapter XXVI: Rama's Mission Fulfilled

text: Clouded was the brow of Rama; he spoke sternly, and said: “Mine enemies are slain, and thou art delivered from captivity, O Sita; but now that my shame is removed I have no desire to behold thee. I cannot receive thee as my wife, because that thou hast dwelt in the house of Ravana.”
chapter_title: Chapter XXVI: Rama's Mission Fulfilled
source_reference: Indian Myth and Legend (Mackenzie 1913), Ch 27, Para 72

metadata.chapter_title: Chapter XXVI: Rama's Mission Fulfilled

text: Said Sita: “Chaste and innocent have I remained.... O Rama, if thou hadst informed me of thy doubt, I would have died ere now. Better is death than thy dark suspicion.”
chapter_title: Chapter XXVI: Rama's Mission Fulfilled
source_reference: Indian Myth and Legend (Mackenzie 1913), Ch 27, Para 73

metadata.chapter_title: Chapter XXVI: Rama's Mission Fulfilled

text: Addressing Lakshmana, she then said: “Build for me a funeral pyre so that I may end my grief amidst the flames.”
chapter_title: Chapter XXVI: Rama's Mission Fulfilled
source_reference: Indian Myth and Legend (Mackenzie 1913), Ch 27, Para 74

metadata.chapter_title: Chapter XXVI: Rama's Mission Fulfilled

text: As she desired so did the brother of Rama do. He built the pyre and set it alight. Then Sita invoked Agni:
chapter_title: Chapter XXVI: Rama's Mission Fulfilled
source_reference: Indian Myth and Legend (Mackenzie 1913), Ch 27, Para 75

metadata.chapter_title: Chapter XXVI: Rama's Mission Fulfilled

text: If in act and thought, she uttered, I am true unto my name, Witness of our sins and virtues, may this fire protect my fame!
chapter_title: Chapter XXVI: Rama's Mission Fulfilled
source_reference: Indian Myth and Legend (Mackenzie 1913), Ch 27, Para 76

metadata.chapter_title: Chapter XXVI: Rama's Mission Fulfilled

text: If a false and lying scandal brings a faithful woman shame, Witness of our sins and virtues, may this fire protect my fame!
chapter_title: Chapter XXVI: Rama's Mission Fulfilled
source_reference: Indian Myth and Legend (Mackenzie 1913), Ch 27, Para 77

metadata.chapter_title: Chapter XXVI: Rama's Mission Fulfilled

text: If in lifelong loving duty I am free from sin and blame, Witness of our sins and virtues, may this fire protect my fame!
chapter_title: Chapter XXVI: Rama's Mission Fulfilled
source_reference: Indian Myth and Legend (Mackenzie 1913), Ch 27, Para 78

metadata.chapter_title: Chapter XXVI: Rama's Mission Fulfilled

text: Fearlessly she then leapt amidst the flames and vanished, while all lamented around her. Rama cried: “This day have I sinned, because she is innocent.”
chapter_title: Chapter XXVI: Rama's Mission Fulfilled
source_reference: Indian Myth and Legend (Mackenzie 1913), Ch 27, Para 79

metadata.chapter_title: Chapter XXVI: Rama's Mission Fulfilled

text: In that hour a great wonder was wrought. Suddenly the Deva-rishis and Gandharvas and the gods appeared in the air. At the same time the red flames of the mighty pyre were divided, and the god Agni came forth with Sita, whom he delivered to Rama, saying: “_Receive thy wife who is without sin or shame._”
chapter_title: Chapter XXVI: Rama's Mission Fulfilled
source_reference: Indian Myth and Legend (Mackenzie 1913), Ch 27, Para 80

metadata.chapter_title: Chapter XXVI: Rama's Mission Fulfilled

text: Rama embraced Sita, and said: “I have never doubted her virtue; she is without sin, and now her purity has been proved before all men.”
chapter_title: Chapter XXVI: Rama's Mission Fulfilled
source_reference: Indian Myth and Legend (Mackenzie 1913), Ch 27, Para 81

metadata.chapter_title: Chapter XXVI: Rama's Mission Fulfilled

text: He wept, and Sita hid her face in his bosom and soft embrace.
chapter_title: Chapter XXVI: Rama's Mission Fulfilled
source_reference: Indian Myth and Legend (Mackenzie 1913), Ch 27, Para 82

metadata.chapter_title: Chapter XXVI: Rama's Mission Fulfilled

text: The exile of Rama was now ended, and he returned speedily in the car of Indra to Ayodhya, with Sita and Lakshmana and Hanuman.
chapter_title: Chapter XXVI: Rama's Mission Fulfilled
source_reference: Indian Myth and Legend (Mackenzie 1913), Ch 27, Para 83

metadata.chapter_title: Chapter XXVI: Rama's Mission Fulfilled

text: Bharata welcomed his elder brother, and laid the sandals at his feet, saying: “These are the symbols of thy rule, O Rama; I have guarded the throne for thee. Now take thy crown and govern thy kingdom. I give thee back thine own.”
chapter_title: Chapter XXVI: Rama's Mission Fulfilled
source_reference: Indian Myth and Legend (Mackenzie 1913), Ch 27, Para 84

metadata.chapter_title: Chapter XXVI: Rama's Mission Fulfilled

text: Rama was crowned on the morrow amidst the rejoicings of the people, and prosperity returned once again to the kingdom.
chapter_title: Chapter XXVI: Rama's Mission Fulfilled
source_reference: Indian Myth and Legend (Mackenzie 1913), Ch 27, Para 85

metadata.chapter_title: Chapter XXVI: Rama's Mission Fulfilled

text: Time went past, but the sorrows of Sita were not ended. The people whispered against the fair queen, doubting her virtue, because that she had been taken away by Ravana, and they wondered Rama had received her back. At length her husband, yielding to the wishes of his subjects, banished the innocent queen from the kingdom. The faithful Lakshmana conducted her towards the southern jungles, and abandoned her nigh to the hermitage of Valmiki, counselling her with tears to take refuge with the saintly poet.
chapter_title: Chapter XXVI: Rama's Mission Fulfilled
source_reference: Indian Myth and Legend (Mackenzie 1913), Ch 27, Para 86

metadata.chapter_title: Chapter XXVI: Rama's Mission Fulfilled

text: Valmiki received her with pity, and soon afterwards she gave birth to two sons, who were named Lava and Kusa.
chapter_title: Chapter XXVI: Rama's Mission Fulfilled
source_reference: Indian Myth and Legend (Mackenzie 1913), Ch 27, Para 87

metadata.chapter_title: Chapter XXVI: Rama's Mission Fulfilled

text: Sixteen years went past, and Rama's mind was troubled because that he had slain Ravana, who was the son of Pulastya, the Rishi. So he resolved to perform the Aswamedha (horse sacrifice) to cleanse his soul of sin.
chapter_title: Chapter XXVI: Rama's Mission Fulfilled
source_reference: Indian Myth and Legend (Mackenzie 1913), Ch 27, Para 88

metadata.chapter_title: Chapter XXVI: Rama's Mission Fulfilled

text: The horse was sent forth to wander through the land, and when it approached the hermitage of Valmiki, Lava and Kusa, the sons of Rama and Sita, took possession of it. They defeated the royal army and wounded Satrughna. Lakshmana hastened forth with another army, but he was also grievously wounded and defeated by the young heroes. Then Rama himself went southward to wage war and recapture the horse. When his sons came forth against him, Rama wondered to find that they were so like to himself in countenance and bearing; his heart was filled with tenderness, and he asked them: “Whose children are you?”
chapter_title: Chapter XXVI: Rama's Mission Fulfilled
source_reference: Indian Myth and Legend (Mackenzie 1913), Ch 27, Para 89

metadata.chapter_title: Chapter XXVI: Rama's Mission Fulfilled

text: Lava and Kusa greeted him with reverence, and said: “Sita is our mother, but we know not the name of our sire.”
chapter_title: Chapter XXVI: Rama's Mission Fulfilled
source_reference: Indian Myth and Legend (Mackenzie 1913), Ch 27, Para 90

metadata.chapter_title: Chapter XXVI: Rama's Mission Fulfilled

text: Then Rama perceived that the lads were his own sons.... Valmiki, the sage, came towards him, and Rama said: “The people spoke evil things against Sita, and it was necessary to prove her innocence. Now let her be taken into my presence, for I know that these noble children are mine.”
chapter_title: Chapter XXVI: Rama's Mission Fulfilled
source_reference: Indian Myth and Legend (Mackenzie 1913), Ch 27, Para 91

metadata.chapter_title: Chapter XXVI: Rama's Mission Fulfilled

text: Valmiki returned to Sita and asked her to go with him before Rama, but for a time she refused to do so. The sage pleaded with her, and at length she walked forth from the hermitage with downcast eyes and hands uplifted. In the presence of Rama and the people she then invoked the Earth, and cried:
chapter_title: Chapter XXVI: Rama's Mission Fulfilled
source_reference: Indian Myth and Legend (Mackenzie 1913), Ch 27, Para 92

metadata.chapter_title: Chapter XXVI: Rama's Mission Fulfilled

text: If unstained in thought and action I have lived from day of birth, Spare a daughter's shame and anguish and receive her, Mother Earth!
chapter_title: Chapter XXVI: Rama's Mission Fulfilled
source_reference: Indian Myth and Legend (Mackenzie 1913), Ch 27, Para 93

metadata.chapter_title: Chapter XXVI: Rama's Mission Fulfilled

text: If in duty and devotion I have laboured undefiled, Mother Earth! who bore this woman, once again receive thy child!
chapter_title: Chapter XXVI: Rama's Mission Fulfilled
source_reference: Indian Myth and Legend (Mackenzie 1913), Ch 27, Para 94

metadata.chapter_title: Chapter XXVI: Rama's Mission Fulfilled

text: If in truth unto my husband I have proved a faithful wife, Mother Earth! relieve thy Sita from the burden of this life!
chapter_title: Chapter XXVI: Rama's Mission Fulfilled
source_reference: Indian Myth and Legend (Mackenzie 1913), Ch 27, Para 95

metadata.chapter_title: Chapter XXVI: Rama's Mission Fulfilled

text: When she had spoken thus, all who heard her wept and sorrowed. And while they gazed upon her with pity and tenderness, the earth suddenly yawned, and from its depths arose a golden throne sparkling with gems and supported by four great serpents, as a rose is supported by green leaves. Then the Earth Mother appeared and hailed Sita with loving words, and led her to the throne, on which she seated herself beside her sinless daughter, the faithful and undefiled wife of Rama.... The throne thereafter vanished and the earth closed over it.
chapter_title: Chapter XXVI: Rama's Mission Fulfilled
source_reference: Indian Myth and Legend (Mackenzie 1913), Ch 27, Para 96

metadata.chapter_title: Chapter XXVI: Rama's Mission Fulfilled

text: So passed Sita from before the eyes of all mankind. Rama flung himself upon the ground in an agony of sorrow. But Brahma appeared and spake to him, saying: “Why dost thou despair, O Lord of all? Well thou knowest that life is but a dream, a bubble of water....”
chapter_title: Chapter XXVI: Rama's Mission Fulfilled
source_reference: Indian Myth and Legend (Mackenzie 1913), Ch 27, Para 97

metadata.chapter_title: Chapter XXVI: Rama's Mission Fulfilled

text: Rama, however, even after the Aswamedha had been performed, continued to mourn until the Celestial bird Garuda came for him: then he ascended to heaven, as Vishnu, and found Sita, who was the goddess Lakshmi, the incomparable Sri.
chapter_title: Chapter XXVI: Rama's Mission Fulfilled
source_reference: Indian Myth and Legend (Mackenzie 1913), Ch 27, Para 98

metadata.chapter_title: Chapter XXVI: Rama's Mission Fulfilled

text: So endeth the story of Rama, whose fame can never die.
chapter_title: Chapter XXVI: Rama's Mission Fulfilled
source_reference: Indian Myth and Legend (Mackenzie 1913), Ch 27, Para 99

metadata.chapter_title: Chapter XXVI: Rama's Mission Fulfilled
